The task pipeline window's current-stage block — before and after

gui-improve pipeline, row #260, stage 1 baseline live · visit 1 · stage run gui-improve/baseline#1 · the same fixture, the same steps and the same four viewports on both sides.

improved 4 viewport pairs · 19/19 unit checks · 66/66 live checks

The defect: the visit span is a grid child the placement rule never named, so the row's auto-placement cursor drops it into the 18 px ordinal column. It paints across the elapsed line — visit and in this stage interleave as visin this stage — and the rest of it wraps one fragment per line. The fix names it (and the decision line, the only other unnamed child) in the rule that gives every line under the title grid-column: 2 / -1.

1440x900 card 780 × 693.72 → 780 × 639.2 · 164198 px changed (32.94% of the 780×639 pair)

the card is 693.72px tall before and 639.2px after: the defect wrapped the visit line into 4 painted lines, so the fix removes 54.52px of block height. Both shots are the same 780px-wide card; the diff is the common top region (780x639), never a padded or rescaled copy.

+.pipew-phase, .pipew-live, .pipew-visit, .pipew-decision, .pipew-artifact, .pipew-gate | grid-column: 2 / -1; font-size: 10px; color: var(--dim);

48 → 48 matched rules; 1 added, 1 removed.

Guards

  • every viewport: the visit line, the clock and the artifact line each own a line, nothing paints outside its box, the element set and control names are unchanged, the only text that moved is the live clock, and both test runs are green
